messages:
alice: Quick question — this PR touches runtime/scheduler/sched.go and docs/deploy.md. Who can approve? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4823
ben: CODEOWNERS should route runtime files to @eng-runtime-maintainers and docs to @docs-team. That means you probably need reviewers from both groups.
carla: For tiny doc fixes we sometimes let the code owner sign off both, but since runtime code changed you definitely need an eng-runtime approval. Our rule: runtime code changes require 2 approvers, one must be from eng-runtime.
alice: Got it. Is that spelled out somewhere (CONTRIBUTING or a team doc)?
ben: Yes — CONTRIBUTING.md in repo root. It has the snippet:
```
Changes to runtime require 2 approvers; at least one must be from @eng-runtime-maintainers.
Docs-only changes can be approved by @docs-team.
```
carla: Also consider perf/security reviewers depending on the change. If sched.go touches batching logic, ping @perf-sig. Add label `needs-perf-review` if you want eyeballs.
dev-bot: reviewbot: Reviewers auto-requested: @eng-runtime-maintainers, @docs-team
drew: If CODEOWNERS didn't pick up the docs reviewer for some reason, manually add someone from @docs-team in the PR. You can also add @eng-platform as a fallback for coordination.
emily: There's also an `OWNERS_OVERRIDE` pattern in urgent cases — add a line in the PR description and an infra lead needs to ack it (used rarely).
ben: Merge checklist: CI green, 2 approvals (incl. eng-runtime), changelog updated. For urgent bugfixes add label `urgent` and mention release lead for expedited merge.
carla: TL;DR: Add eng-runtime reviewer, add docs reviewer, label `needs-perf-review` if relevant, wait for 2 approvals, then merge. Ping me if it stalls and I'll help nudge. :thumbsup:
alice: Thanks all — I'll add reviewers now and tag @carla if it blocks.
